title: The Man Who Moved Continents
subtitle: 移動大陸的人：韋格納與大陸漂移說
source: 原創議題文章；依 Wikipedia〈Alfred Wegener〉〈Continental drift〉與 NASA Earth Observatory〈Alfred Wegener〉核對，2026-10-22

beginner.title: A Jigsaw Puzzle of Continents
paras: Look at a world map. Do South America and Africa look like two pieces of a jigsaw puzzle? A German scientist called Alfred Wegener noticed this too. In 1912 he said something shocking: long ago, all the continents were joined together, and since then they have slowly moved apart.
看看世界地圖。南美洲和非洲是不是很像兩片拼圖？德國科學家阿爾弗雷德．韋格納也注意到了。1912 年，他提出一個驚人的說法：很久以前，所有大陸都連在一起，之後才慢慢分開。

Wegener found more clues. Fossils of the same ancient animals and plants were found on continents that are now far apart. For example, fossils of a small reptile called Mesosaurus were found in both Brazil and South Africa. It could not swim across an ocean, so how did it get there?
韋格納找到了更多線索。同樣的古代動植物化石，出現在如今相隔遙遠的大陸上。例如，一種叫中龍的小型爬蟲類化石，在巴西和南非都有發現。牠不可能游過大洋，那牠是怎麼到那裡的？

Most geologists laughed at his idea. Wegener was a weather scientist, not a geologist, so many experts saw him as an outsider. Also, he could not explain what force could move giant continents. His guesses about the force were wrong.
大多數地質學家都嘲笑他的想法。韋格納是氣象學家，不是地質學家，所以很多專家把他當成圈外人。而且，他無法解釋是什麼力量能移動巨大的大陸。他對這股力量的猜測也是錯的。

In 1930, Wegener died on a trip across the ice in Greenland. He was 50 years old. At that time, most scientists still did not believe him. He never knew that he would one day be proved right. His companion, a young Greenlander called Rasmus Villumsen, was never seen again. Wegener’s skis, standing upright in the snow, helped searchers find his body.
1930 年，韋格納在格陵蘭的冰原旅程中過世，享年 50 歲。當時，大多數科學家仍然不相信他。他永遠不知道，自己有一天會被證明是對的。他的同伴，一位名叫拉斯穆斯．維倫森的年輕格陵蘭人，從此再也沒有出現過。韋格納直立插在雪中的滑雪板，幫助搜救人員找到了他的遺體。

In the 1960s, scientists studied the ocean floor and found new evidence. Continents really do move, carried on huge plates. Today this is called plate tectonics. Wegener’s story shows that a new idea can be right even when experts reject it — but it also needs evidence to win.
1960 年代，科學家研究海底，找到了新的證據。大陸真的會移動，是被巨大的板塊載著走。今天這被稱為板塊構造論。韋格納的故事顯示：一個新想法即使被專家否定，也可能是對的——但它也需要證據才能獲勝。

intermediate.title: The Man Who Moved Continents
paras: Anyone who looks at a world map may notice that the coasts of South America and Africa fit together almost like pieces of a jigsaw puzzle. On 6 January 1912, the German scientist Alfred Wegener presented a bold explanation: all the continents had once been joined in a single landmass, which later broke apart. In 1915 he set out his argument in a book, The Origin of Continents and Oceans. He was not the very first to wonder about this; the mapmaker Abraham Ortelius had suggested in 1596 that the continents might have drifted. But Wegener developed the idea far more fully.
任何看過世界地圖的人，都可能注意到南美洲和非洲的海岸線幾乎能像拼圖一樣拼在一起。1912 年 1 月 6 日，德國科學家阿爾弗雷德．韋格納提出一個大膽的解釋：所有大陸曾經連成一整塊陸地，之後才分裂開來。1915 年，他在《大陸與海洋的起源》一書中闡述了這個論點。他並不是第一個想到這件事的人；地圖學家亞伯拉罕．奧特柳斯早在 1596 年就曾提出大陸可能漂移過。但韋格納把這個想法發展得完整得多。

His evidence went beyond the shapes of coastlines. He compared rocks, geological structures and fossils on both sides of the Atlantic and found striking similarities. Fossils of Mesosaurus, a freshwater reptile rather like a small crocodile, have been found in both Brazil and South Africa — an unlikely result if the two continents had always been separated by an ocean.
他的證據不只是海岸線的形狀。他比較了大西洋兩岸的岩石、地質構造和化石，發現了驚人的相似之處。中龍——一種有點像小鱷魚的淡水爬蟲類——的化石在巴西和南非都有發現；如果這兩塊大陸一直被大洋隔開，這幾乎不可能發生。

Yet most experts rejected the idea, often with withering criticism. Part of the problem was who Wegener was: a meteorologist and polar researcher whom many geologists regarded as an outsider. But the critics also had a fair point. Wegener could not identify a mechanism powerful enough to move continents, and his suggestions — such as forces linked to the Earth’s rotation — were wrong.
然而，大多數專家否定了這個想法，批評往往十分尖刻。部分問題出在韋格納的身分：他是氣象學家和極地研究者，許多地質學家把他視為圈外人。但批評者也有一個合理的論點：韋格納找不到一個強大到足以移動大陸的機制，而他提出的說法——例如與地球自轉有關的力——是錯的。

Wegener did not live to see his idea accepted. In November 1930, during an expedition across the Greenland ice sheet, he set out with a young Greenlander, Rasmus Villumsen, to return to the coast. Wegener died on the way, probably of heart failure caused by exhaustion. His body was found the following May. Sadly, it was later found that there had been enough supplies for them to stay at the central station.
韋格納沒能活著看到自己的想法被接受。1930 年 11 月，在一次橫越格陵蘭冰原的探險中，他和年輕的格陵蘭人拉斯穆斯．維倫森一起出發返回海岸。韋格納在途中過世，很可能是過度勞累引發的心臟衰竭。隔年五月，他的遺體才被發現。令人遺憾的是，後來發現中央站其實有足夠的補給讓他們留下來。

The decisive evidence arrived decades later. In the late 1950s and 1960s, studies of the ocean floor revealed zebra-like stripes of magnetism and showed that new sea floor was being created along mid-ocean ridges. Continental drift became part of the theory of plate tectonics. Wegener’s story is a reminder that being right too early is not enough: a new idea also needs a convincing mechanism and the evidence to prove it.
決定性的證據在幾十年後才出現。1950 年代末到 1960 年代，對海底的研究揭露了斑馬紋般的磁性條帶，並顯示新的海床正沿著中洋脊不斷生成。大陸漂移成為板塊構造論的一部分。韋格納的故事提醒我們：太早說對還不夠；一個新想法也需要令人信服的機制，以及證明它的證據。

advanced.title: Right Too Early: Wegener and the Burden of Proof
paras: The history of science is often told as a contest between brave innovators and stubborn establishments, and Alfred Wegener seems to fit the pattern perfectly. On 6 January 1912 he proposed that the continents had once formed a single landmass, later called Pangaea, which had broken apart and drifted into its present configuration. Expanded in 1915 as The Origin of Continents and Oceans, the hypothesis was not accepted by mainstream geology until the 1960s. Yet a closer look suggests that the story of Wegener’s rejection is more instructive than a simple tale of prejudice. He was not the first to speculate along these lines — the cartographer Abraham Ortelius had done so in 1596 — but he developed the idea most fully.

科學史常被講成勇敢的創新者對抗頑固體制的競賽，而阿爾弗雷德．韋格納似乎完美符合這個模式。1912 年 1 月 6 日，他提出各大陸曾構成單一陸塊——後來稱為「盤古大陸」——之後分裂、漂移成今天的樣貌。這個假說在 1915 年擴寫成《大陸與海洋的起源》，卻直到 1960 年代才被主流地質學接受。然而，仔細檢視會發現，韋格納遭到否定的故事，比一個單純的偏見故事更有啟發性。他並不是第一個這樣推測的人——地圖學家奧特柳斯早在 1596 年就提過——但他把這個想法發展得最完整。

Wegener’s case was impressively interdisciplinary. Beyond the jigsaw-like fit of the Atlantic coastlines, he compared rock types, geological structures and fossils on opposite sides of the ocean. Fossils of Mesosaurus, a freshwater reptile, appear in both Brazil and South Africa, while remains of the land reptile Lystrosaurus occur in rocks of the same age in Africa, India and Antarctica. He offered a memorable analogy: it was as if one were to refit the torn pieces of a newspaper and check whether the lines of print ran smoothly across.
韋格納的論證具有令人印象深刻的跨領域性。除了大西洋海岸線像拼圖般的吻合，他還比較了大洋兩岸的岩石種類、地質構造和化石。淡水爬蟲類中龍的化石，同時出現在巴西和南非；陸生爬蟲類水龍獸的遺骸，則出現在非洲、印度和南極洲同年代的岩層中。他提出一個令人難忘的比喻：這就像把撕碎的報紙拼回去，再檢查印刷的字行是否能順暢地連起來。

The response was largely hostile. Many geologists regarded Wegener, a meteorologist and polar researcher, as an outsider, and when he presented the theory at a 1926 symposium of the American Association of Petroleum Geologists in New York, it was rejected by almost everyone except the chairman. Some criticism was undoubtedly defensive. But the strongest objection was scientifically legitimate: there was no known mechanism capable of propelling continents across the globe. Wegener’s own proposals, involving centrifugal force from the Earth’s rotation and astronomical precession, were inadequate.
回應大多充滿敵意。許多地質學家把身為氣象學家和極地研究者的韋格納視為圈外人；1926 年他在紐約美國石油地質學家協會的研討會上發表這個理論時，除了主席以外幾乎所有人都否定了它。有些批評無疑是出於防衛心態。但最有力的反對意見在科學上是正當的：當時沒有已知的機制，能推動大陸在全球移動。韋格納自己提出的機制——涉及地球自轉的離心力和天文歲差——並不足以解釋。

Ironically, the elements of a solution were already emerging. In 1931 the English geologist Arthur Holmes proposed mantle convection as a possible driving force, and Wegener himself had speculated about the role of mid-ocean ridges. He did not live to see these ideas developed. In November 1930, while leaving the central station of his Greenland expedition with Rasmus Villumsen, he died on the ice sheet, probably of heart failure brought on by overexertion. His body was not found until May 1931.
諷刺的是，解答的元素其實已經開始浮現。1931 年，英國地質學家亞瑟．霍姆斯提出地函對流可能是驅動力，而韋格納自己也曾推測中洋脊的作用。他沒能活著看到這些想法被發展出來。1930 年 11 月，他和拉斯穆斯．維倫森離開格陵蘭探險隊的中央站後，死在冰原上，很可能是過度勞累引發的心臟衰竭。他的遺體直到 1931 年 5 月才被發現。

Vindication came from the ocean floor. Between 1959 and 1963, researchers found that the sea floor carried zebra-like stripes of alternating magnetic polarity, best explained by new crust forming at mid-ocean ridges and spreading outward. Continental drift was absorbed into the broader theory of plate tectonics. The lesson is subtler than “the experts were wrong”. Wegener’s critics were wrong about his conclusion but right to demand a mechanism. Science advanced not by deferring to authority or rewarding boldness alone, but by insisting on evidence until it finally arrived.
平反來自海底。1959 到 1963 年間，研究者發現海床上帶有磁極方向交替的斑馬紋條帶，最好的解釋是新的地殼在中洋脊生成並向外擴張。大陸漂移被納入更廣泛的板塊構造論。這個教訓比「專家錯了」更細膩：韋格納的批評者在結論上錯了，但要求提出機制卻是對的。科學之所以進步，既不是靠服從權威，也不只是獎勵大膽，而是堅持要求證據，直到證據終於出現。

quote.text: It is just as if we were to refit the torn pieces of a newspaper by matching their edges and then check whether the lines of print ran smoothly across.
quote.author: Alfred Wegener
quote.work: The Origin of Continents and Oceans, as quoted by NASA Earth Observatory

beginner.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How Rasmus Villumsen explored the ice of Greenland.
How to put together a jigsaw puzzle of the world.
Why Mesosaurus was able to swim across the ocean.
A scientist whose rejected idea was later proved right.
beginner.evidence: Wegener’s story shows that a new idea can be right even when experts reject it
beginner.why: 全文：韋格納的大陸漂移說先被否定，後來被證實。
traps: 以偏概全：他只是同行者。
字面誤讀：拼圖只是比喻。
正反顛倒：牠不能游過海洋。

beginner.q: What does “it” in “how did it get there?” in the second paragraph refer to?
options: The ocean between the continents.
Mesosaurus, the small reptile.
The fossil of an ancient plant.
The continent of South Africa.
beginner.evidence: fossils of a small reptile called Mesosaurus were found in both Brazil and South Africa
beginner.why: 前一句：那隻小型爬蟲類不能游過海洋，牠怎麼到那裡的？
traps: 原文字眼、錯誤關係：海洋是牠無法跨越的障礙。
以偏概全：句子說的是 Mesosaurus，不是植物。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：南非是化石被發現的地方。

beginner.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: Most geologists accepted Wegener’s idea at once.
Wegener explained exactly what force moves continents.
Wegener was a weather scientist, not a geologist.
Wegener lived to see his idea proved right.
beginner.evidence: Wegener was a weather scientist, not a geologist
traps: 正反顛倒：多數地質學家嘲笑他。
正反顛倒：他的猜測是錯的。
正反顛倒：他至死都沒被證實。

beginner.q: What does the writer suggest a new idea needs in order to win acceptance?
options: Evidence that supports it.
A famous scientist to present it.
Experts who laugh at it.
A trip across Greenland.
beginner.evidence: but it also needs evidence to win
traps: 捏造：文中沒有。重點是證據。
正反顛倒：被嘲笑不會讓想法被接受。
字面誤讀：格陵蘭是他喪命的地方。

intermediate.q: Which of the following best states the main idea of the passage?
options: Wegener was right, but his idea needed a mechanism and evidence.
Wegener proved continental drift beyond any doubt in 1912.
Abraham Ortelius developed the theory of plate tectonics in 1596.
Wegener’s critics had no good reason at all to doubt him.
intermediate.evidence: a new idea also needs a convincing mechanism and the evidence to prove it
traps: 正反顛倒：當時被多數專家否定。
張冠李戴：Ortelius 只是早期提出漂移的可能。
正反顛倒：批評者指出缺乏機制，有其道理。

intermediate.q: What does “withering criticism” in the third paragraph most likely mean?
options: Criticism that slowly disappears.
Gentle and helpful advice.
Very harsh criticism.
Praise hidden in a complaint.
intermediate.evidence: Yet most experts rejected the idea, often with withering criticism.
intermediate.why: 多數專家否定這個想法，而且批評尖銳。
traps: 字面誤讀：wither 是枯萎，但這裡形容批評很狠。
正反顛倒：他們是強烈反對。
捏造：文中沒有讚美。

intermediate.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: Wegener died in January 1912 in Greenland.
Wegener’s body was found the May after he died.
Mesosaurus was a large saltwater reptile.
Wegener published his book in 1930.
intermediate.evidence: His body was found the following May.
traps: 時序錯置：1912 年是發表想法的日子，他 1930 年 11 月過世。
正反顛倒：是淡水的小型爬蟲類。
數字錯位：書是 1915 年出版。

intermediate.q: What does the discovery about supplies at the central station suggest?
options: The expedition was cancelled before it began.
The station had run out of food completely.
Villumsen had taken all the supplies with him.
Wegener’s final journey may not have been necessary.
intermediate.evidence: there had been enough supplies for them to stay at the central station
intermediate.why: 第四段：原本留在站上也夠用，令人惋惜。
traps: 正反顛倒：遠征已經進行中。
正反顛倒：補給其實足夠。
捏造：文中沒說 Villumsen 帶走補給。

advanced.q: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To prove that the geologists of the 1920s were simply prejudiced.
To show that Wegener’s story is more complex than it seems.
To describe the life and work of Arthur Holmes in detail.
To explain how newspapers were printed in the 1910s.
advanced.evidence: The lesson is subtler than “the experts were wrong”.
advanced.why: 最後一段：批評者錯在結論，但要求機制是對的。
traps: 以偏概全：作者說有些批評是防衛性的，但最強的反對有道理。
以偏概全：Holmes 只出現在第四段。
字面誤讀：報紙只是 Wegener 的比喻。

advanced.q: What is the point of Wegener’s analogy about the torn pieces of a newspaper?
options: Fossils were first described in old newspapers.
Newspapers should report scientific discoveries much more often.
Continents tear apart as easily as pieces of paper.
Matching continents is like checking that printed lines meet.
advanced.evidence: it was as if one were to refit the torn pieces of a newspaper and check whether the lines of print ran smoothly across
advanced.why: 第二段：拼回撕碎的報紙、看字行是否連得起來，就像比對兩岸的岩石與化石。
traps: 捏造：化石出現在岩石中。
捏造：文中沒有。這只是比喻。
字面誤讀：重點在比對，不在撕裂的難易。

advanced.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: At the 1926 symposium, almost everyone except the chairman rejected the theory.
Arthur Holmes proposed mantle convection in 1915.
Lystrosaurus fossils were found only in Brazil.
Magnetic stripes on the sea floor were found in the 1920s.
advanced.evidence: it was rejected by almost everyone except the chairman
traps: 數字錯位：1931 年。
張冠李戴：Lystrosaurus 在非洲、印度和南極洲。
時序錯置：1959 到 1963 年才發現。

advanced.q: According to the author, which objection to Wegener was scientifically legitimate?
options: He presented his theory in New York.
He was a meteorologist rather than a geologist.
There was no known mechanism that could move the continents.
He was not the first to suggest continental drift.
advanced.evidence: there was no known mechanism capable of propelling continents across the globe
advanced.why: 第三段：最有力的反對是沒有已知的驅動機制。
traps: 原文字眼、錯誤關係：紐約只是研討會地點。
張冠李戴：說他是外行是偏見，不是科學理由。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：Ortelius 更早提過，但這不是反對的理由。

reflections: Compare Wegener with John Harrison (the longitude article). Both were outsiders. How were their stories similar and different?
Is it fair for experts to reject an idea that has no explanation for how it works? Give your opinion.

He set out the idea in 1915 in The Origin of Continents and Oceans, yet mainstream geology did not accept it until the 1960s. A closer look, however, suggests a more instructive story.
科學史常被講成勇敢的圈外人對抗頑固專家的故事，而韋格納似乎完全符合這個模式。1912 年 1 月 6 日，這位德國科學家提出：各大陸曾經是一整塊陸地，後來裂開並漂移到現在的位置。他在 1915 年的《大陸與海洋的起源》中闡述這個想法，但主流地質學界直到 1960 年代才接受。然而仔細一看，這個故事能帶來更多啟發。

Wegener was not the first to wonder about drifting continents; the mapmaker Abraham Ortelius had suggested it in 1596. But he developed the idea far more fully. Beyond the jigsaw-like fit of the Atlantic coastlines, he compared rocks, geological structures and fossils on both sides of the ocean. Fossils of Mesosaurus, a freshwater reptile, appear in both Brazil and South Africa — an unlikely result if the two continents had always been separated by an ocean. It was, he said, as if one were checking whether the lines of print ran smoothly across the torn pieces of a newspaper.
韋格納並不是第一個想到大陸會漂移的人；製圖師奧特柳斯在 1596 年就提過。但他把這個想法發展得完整得多。除了大西洋兩岸海岸線像拼圖般吻合，他還比對了大洋兩側的岩石、地質構造和化石。淡水爬蟲類中龍的化石，同時出現在巴西和南非——如果兩塊大陸一直隔著海洋，這是不太可能的。他說，這就像拼回撕碎的報紙，檢查字行是否能順暢地連起來。

The response was largely hostile. Many geologists saw Wegener, a meteorologist (a scientist who studies weather) and polar researcher, as an outsider. When he presented the theory at a 1926 meeting in New York, it was rejected by almost everyone except the chairman. Some of the criticism was undoubtedly defensive. Yet the strongest objection was scientifically fair: no known force could push continents across the globe, and Wegener’s own suggestions, such as forces from the Earth’s rotation, were inadequate.
反應大多充滿敵意。許多地質學家把身為氣象學家（研究天氣的科學家）兼極地研究者的韋格納看成外行人。他在 1926 年紐約的一場會議上發表這個理論時，除了主席之外，幾乎所有人都反對。有些批評無疑帶著防衛心。然而最有力的反對在科學上是合理的：沒有任何已知的力量能推動大陸橫越地球，而韋格納自己提出的解釋，例如來自地球自轉的力量，都不夠充分。

Ironically, part of a solution was already emerging. In 1931, the English geologist Arthur Holmes proposed slow movements deep inside the Earth as a possible driving force. Wegener did not live to see such ideas developed. In November 1930, while leaving a station on the Greenland ice sheet with Rasmus Villumsen, he died, probably of heart failure brought on by exhaustion. So harsh were the conditions that his body was not found until May 1931.
諷刺的是，解答的一部分其實已經浮現。1931 年，英國地質學家霍姆斯提出，地球深處的緩慢運動可能就是驅動力。韋格納沒能活著看到這些想法發展起來。1930 年 11 月，他和維盧姆森離開格陵蘭冰原上的一個站時去世，很可能是過度疲勞引發心臟衰竭。當地條件惡劣到他的遺體直到 1931 年 5 月才被找到。

Not until the ocean floor was studied did proof arrive. Between 1959 and 1963, researchers found that the sea floor carried zebra-like stripes of magnetism, best explained by new crust forming at mid-ocean ridges and spreading outward. Continental drift became part of the wider theory of plate tectonics. The lesson is subtler than “the experts were wrong”: Wegener’s critics were wrong about his conclusion but right to demand a mechanism. Science advanced not by rewarding boldness alone, but by insisting on evidence until it finally came.
直到研究了海底，證據才出現。1959 到 1963 年間，研究者發現海底帶有斑馬紋般的磁性條帶，最好的解釋是新的地殼在中洋脊形成並向外擴張。大陸漂移成了更廣泛的板塊構造理論的一部分。教訓比「專家錯了」更細膩：批評韋格納的人在結論上錯了，但要求他提出機制是對的。科學的進步不是光靠獎勵大膽，而是堅持要證據，直到證據終於出現。
